title: Fixed-width integer types and format macros from stdint.h/inttypes.h
learningObjectives: Explain the topic and its C rules.
Trace the example and explain its data or control flow.

understand.concept: stdint.h provides optional exact-width and minimum-width integer types such as int32_t and uint_least16_t where supported. inttypes.h provides format macros such as PRId32 for printing fixed-width types portably.
understand.whyItMatters: Using the correct type and matching format macro avoids assumptions about the width of int, long or long long across platforms.
understand.analogy: Treat each algorithm or resource as a contract whose invariants must remain true after every operation.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: PRId32 expands to the appropriate format fragment for int32_t on the implementation. The format string joins it with the surrounding literal text.

practise.guidedTask: Explain why %d is not the universal format for every fixed-width integer typedef.
practise.independentTask: Print signed and unsigned fixed-width values using the corresponding inttypes.h macros.
hints: Exact-width typedefs are optional when an implementation lacks the exact representation.
Use the format macro that matches the actual argument type.
Do not assume a typedef's underlying type from its name.
